lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 141: Ctrl+F searches this folder, and Ctrl+Shift+F includes its subfolders.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one forty-one: Control F searches this folder, and Control Shift F includes its subfolders.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Two shortcuts now choose a search's scope and save it on the folder, as a click on the Include subfolders toggle does.
Ctrl+F, or Search for Files in the Go menu, now searches only the folder you're in.
lines.say: Control F, or Search for Files in the Go menu, now searches only the folder you're in.

lines.caption: Ctrl+Shift+F is new: it searches the folder and all its subfolders, and you can rebind it.
lines.say: Control Shift F is new: it searches the folder and all its subfolders, and you can rebind it.

lines.caption: Before the search starts, the shortcut saves its scope on the folder, with the same call a toggle click makes.
The search opens with the toggle showing that scope, and the results follow it.
Pressing either shortcut during a search ends it, as Ctrl+F did before.
lines.say: Pressing either shortcut during a search ends it, as Control F did before.

lines.caption: The toolbar Search button and the Search key work as before.
They open with the folder's saved choice, or the global preference in a folder never searched.
Since issue 21, Thunar remembers the scope per folder, but Ctrl+F always used it, so changing it needed the mouse.
lines.say: Since issue twenty-one, Thunar remembers the scope per folder, but Control F always used it, so changing it needed the mouse.

lines.caption: A shortcut saves its scope on the folder, so the toolbar button later opens with the scope you used there last.
The toggle now re-reads the folder's choice on every change to the search text, a fix from the local review.
The toolbar button is built from the Ctrl+F action, so the PR gives it its own saved-choice handler.
lines.say: The toolbar button is built from the Control F action, so the pull request gives it its own saved-choice handler.

lines.caption: This table lists every way to open a search, what it searches, and what it saves on the folder.
The core of the change: unless the scope is the saved one, it's written to the folder before the search opens.
One helper takes the scope: folder, subfolders, or saved, which skips the save.
After a search typed by hand, a shortcut starts a new one, and the toggle now updates to match it.
The PR changes three source files, adds a verify script, updates two others, and adds this page.
To undo it, revert the PR. Scopes already saved stay on the folders, where the toggle saves them too.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was tested twice by the full verify suite in the cloud container, its shots audited, and reviewed locally. CI runs after the push.
lines.say: It was tested twice by the full verify suite in the cloud container, its shots audited, and reviewed locally. C I runs after the push.

lines.caption: It reuses the toggle's save call from issue 21 and copies the existing Ctrl+F action.
lines.say: It reuses the toggle's save call from issue twenty-one and copies the existing Control F action.

lines.caption: The final code built, and all 30 verify scripts passed in the cloud container.
lines.say: The final code built, and all thirty verify scripts passed in the cloud container.

lines.caption: The new script read the folder's saved scope after each shortcut: off for Ctrl+F, on for Ctrl+Shift+F.
lines.say: The new script read the folder's saved scope after each shortcut: off for Control F, on for Control Shift F.

lines.caption: Ctrl+Shift+F listed both matching files, and a click on the toggle brought it back to the top one.
lines.say: Control Shift F listed both matching files, and a click on the toggle brought it back to the top one.

lines.caption: The toolbar button kept the saved choice, and a shortcut during a search ended it.
An independent auditor read the six screenshots from the first run, before the review fix: all six were right.
That first run failed two older scripts that opened their searches with Ctrl+F. Both were updated, then passed.
lines.say: That first run failed two older scripts that opened their searches with Control F. Both were updated, then passed.

lines.caption: The build showed no compiler warnings in the changed code.
Not run: the toggle after a hand-typed search, split view, a folder without saved metadata, and the video.
The local review at high level found three things before the first push, and one was fixed.
Fixed: after a search typed by hand, the toggle could show the old scope. It now syncs on every text change.
Skipped, for you: without gvfs, a shortcut's scope can be forgotten, as the toggle's already can.
lines.say: Skipped, for you: without G V F S, a shortcut's scope can be forgotten, as the toggle's already can.

lines.caption: The third was the missing explainer, this page. CI's own review reports on the PR after the push.
lines.say: The third was the missing explainer, this page. C I's own review reports on the pull request after the push.

lines.caption: CI's jobs and the audit of its shots run after the push, and the shortcuts reach your Thunar with the next package.
lines.say: C I's jobs and the audit of its shots run after the push, and the shortcuts reach your Thunar with the next package.

lines.caption: The PR, the issue and CI's verify comment with the three shot pairs are linked here.
lines.say: The pull request, the issue and C I's verify comment with the three shot pairs are linked here.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue builds on this one. The local review suggested one possible follow-up.
After this PR, a possible issue could keep a shortcut's scope per window where folders can't save it.
Today, without gvfs, the scope lasts only while Thunar keeps the folder in memory. A per-window override could fix that.
lines.say: Today, without G V F S, the scope lasts only while Thunar keeps the folder in memory. A per-window override could fix that.

lines.caption: It's your call whether to open it as an issue.
In short: Ctrl+F searches the folder you're in, Ctrl+Shift+F adds its subfolders, and the toolbar keeps your last choice.
lines.say: In short: Control F searches the folder you're in, Control Shift F adds its subfolders, and the toolbar keeps your last choice.
